name: Josiah
charge: A tender heart at the reading of the book; turning to the Lord with all his heart, soul, and might, according to all the law of Moses
summary: Eight years old when crowned, sixteen when he began to seek the God of David, twenty when he began to purge Judah, twenty-six when the book of the law was found in the house and read to him. He rent his clothes, gathered the people, read it to them himself, and kept a passover like none since Samuel. He was promised he would be gathered to his grave in peace before the evil came. His death at Megiddo is its own case.
offense: Josiah began seeking the God of David while young, and his purge of idolatry began before the book of the law was found during the temple repairs (2 Chronicles 34:3-8). The discovery deepened an existing course of reform. It did not find him indifferent to the Lord until that day. When the book was read, he rent his clothes and sent to inquire because the fathers had not kept its words. Huldah answered concerning both the coming national judgment and his tender heart (2 Kings 22:11-20). He received the charge as something demanding a response, not an ancient record to be admired without obedience. He gathered the people, read the covenant, and bound himself to keep it with heart and soul. Idols and their places were removed, and Passover was ordered according to the word (2 Kings 23:1-24). Hearing produced public action reaching the temple, the countryside, and the nation's worship.
judgment: Because thine heart was tender, and thou hast humbled thyself before the Lord, when thou heardest what I spake against this place, and hast rent thy clothes, and wept before me; I also have heard thee, saith the Lord. Behold therefore, I will gather thee unto thy fathers, and thou shalt be gathered into thy grave in peace; and thine eyes shall not see all the evil which I will bring upon this place. And like unto him was there no king before him, that turned to the Lord with all his heart, and with all his soul, and with all his might, according to all the law of Moses; neither after him arose there any like him. Sirach: the remembrance of Josias is like the composition of the perfume that is made by the art of the apothecary.
offenseFull: Josiah began seeking the God of David while young, and his purge of idolatry began before the book of the law was found during the temple repairs (2 Chronicles 34:3-8). The discovery deepened an existing course of reform. It did not find him indifferent to the Lord until that day.

When the book was read, he rent his clothes and sent to inquire because the fathers had not kept its words. Huldah answered concerning both the coming national judgment and his tender heart (2 Kings 22:11-20). He received the charge as something demanding a response, not an ancient record to be admired without obedience.

He gathered the people, read the covenant, and bound himself to keep it with heart and soul. Idols and their places were removed, and Passover was ordered according to the word (2 Kings 23:1-24). Hearing produced public action reaching the temple, the countryside, and the nation's worship.
judgmentFull: The Lord acknowledged his humbling and promised that his eyes would not see the evil to come upon the place (2 Kings 22:18-20). The sentence upon Judah remained, but the king's response was not overlooked within it.

No king before him had turned to the Lord with heart, soul, and might as he did according to Moses' law (2 Kings 23:25). The Passover likewise stood apart among the reigns (2 Chronicles 35:18). His later death at Megiddo was grievous and did not remove that testimony. The promise of being spared the approaching devastation and the record of his fatal battle must both be retained; the good of his reign did not make every later decision beyond correction.

entries.commentary: Josiah begins to reign at eight years old and reigns thirty-one years, doing that which is right in the sight of the Most High and walking in all the way of David, turning neither to the right nor the left. In his eighteenth year he sends Shaphan the scribe to Hilkiah the priest to gather the silver brought to the house of the Most High and deliver it to the workmen for repairs. The money is given to carpenters, builders, and masons and for timber and hewn stone, and no reckoning is made with them because they dealt faithfully. Josiah rebuilds and reestablishes what Manasseh and Amon destroyed, and he makes sure the workmen are paid, for by the law the workman is worthy of his hire.

Hilkiah the high priest finds the book of the law in the house of the Most High and gives it to Shaphan, who reads it. Manasseh and Amon were so wicked the very book of the law had been lost. Shaphan reports to the king about the money and the workmen, then tells him Hilkiah delivered him a book, and reads it before the king. When the king hears the words of the book of the law he rends his clothes, for the king was meant to read the law before all the people, which the wicked kings had not done. Josiah commands Hilkiah and his servants to inquire of the Most High for him and the people, for great is the wrath kindled against them because their fathers did not hearken to this book. -

Hilkiah and the king's men go to Huldah the prophetess, who dwells in Jerusalem in the college; there were women among the people who were prophetesses, known by their works. Huldah returns the word of the Most High: He will bring evil upon this place and its inhabitants, all the words of the book, because they forsook Him and burned incense to other gods, and His wrath shall not be quenched. But to Josiah, because his heart was tender and he humbled himself and wept before the Most High, the word is that he shall be gathered to his fathers and to his grave in peace, and his eyes shall not see the evil to come. Because Josiah was righteous, repaired the temple, found the book, and began to keep the commandments again, he found mercy; yet the word spoken against Israel for its sin would still come to pass. --- Topics: [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood)

Josiah gathered all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem, went up to the house of the Most High with the priests, the prophets, and all the people both small and great, and read in their ears all the words of the book of the covenant that was found there. Our forefathers had the Bible; the king read it openly, then stood by a pillar and made a covenant before the Lord to walk after him and keep his commandments, testimonies, and statutes with all their heart and soul. All the people stood to the covenant to perform the words written in the book. -

The king commanded Hilkiah and the priests to bring out of the temple all the vessels made for Baal, for the grove, and for all the host of heaven, and he burned them in the fields of Kidron and carried their ashes to Bethel. He put down the idolatrous priests whom the kings of Judah had ordained to burn incense in the high places and around Jerusalem, and those that burnt incense to Baal, to the sun, the moon, the planets, and all the host of heaven. When Josiah read the law the fear of the Lord came upon him and he saw why the nation was under judgment, just as a person is cut when they first hear the truth and realize what they have been doing wrong. -

He brought the grove out of the house of the Lord to the brook Kidron, burned it, stamped it to powder, and cast the powder on the graves of the children of the people. He broke down the houses of the sodomites that were by the house of the Lord, where the women wove hangings for the grove; there should be no sodomite among the sons of Israel, yet they had grown so bold as to do this wickedness right beside the temple. He brought all the priests out of the cities of Judah and defiled the high places where they had burnt incense, and though the priests of the high places did not come up to the altar, they still ate of the unleavened bread among their brethren.

Josiah defiled Topheth in the valley of the children of Hinnom so that no man might make his son or daughter pass through the fire to Molech. Topheth was the place where the people sacrificed their children, and it had to be defiled because Israel would not stop the evil on its own. -

He took away the horses the kings of Judah had given to the sun and burnt the chariots of the sun with fire. He beat down the altars on the roof of Ahaz's chamber and the altars Manasseh had made in the two courts of the house of the Lord, and cast their dust into the brook Kidron. He defiled the high places Solomon had built for Ashtoreth, Chemosh, and Milcom, the abominations of the Zidonians, Moabites, and Ammonites, and broke in pieces the images, cut down the groves, and filled their places with the bones of men. This is repentance in action: cleaning house, getting rid of every idol and evil that causes a people to go off from the Lord and to fall under punishment. -

Josiah also destroyed the altar and high place at Bethel that Jeroboam had made when he set up the golden calves, burning it and stamping it small to powder. Turning himself, he spied the sepulchres in the mount, took out the bones, and burnt them upon the altar to pollute it, according to the word the man of God had proclaimed. When told which sepulchre belonged to the man of God who prophesied these things, he said to let him alone and let no man move his bones. -

Josiah also took away all the houses of the high places in the cities of Samaria, which the kings of Israel had made to provoke the Lord to anger, and did to them as he had done at Bethel. The northern kingdom had already been carried into captivity by Assyria, so most of the people were gone, yet the idolatrous houses remained. He slew all the priests of the high places upon their altars, burnt men's bones upon them, and returned to Jerusalem.

The king commanded all the people to keep the Passover to the Lord their God as it is written in the book of this covenant. Such a Passover had not been held from the days of the judges nor in all the days of the kings of Israel and Judah, but in the eighteenth year of Josiah this Passover was held in Jerusalem. Reading the book of the law brought the nation back to keeping the appointed feasts in order, just as the feast is kept in order today. -

Josiah also put away the workers with familiar spirits, the wizards, the images, the idols, and all the abominations spied in Judah and Jerusalem, that he might perform the words of the law found by Hilkiah. There was no king before or after him that turned to the Lord with all his heart, soul, and might according to all the law of Moses; he put things in order like a true leader. Nevertheless the Lord did not turn from the fierceness of his great wrath because of the provocations of Manasseh, and said he would remove Judah out of his sight as he had removed Israel and cast off Jerusalem.

Pharaohnechoh king of Egypt went up against the king of Assyria to the river Euphrates, and Josiah went against him and was slain at Megiddo. Josiah got involved in a matter that did not concern him and lost his life in it, a warning not to enter into quarrels that are not one's own. His servants carried him dead in a chariot from Megiddo to Jerusalem and buried him, and the people took Jehoahaz his son and anointed him king in his father's place.

Jehoahaz was twenty three years old and reigned three months in Jerusalem, and did evil in the sight of the Lord according to all his fathers had done. Pharaohnechoh bound him at Riblah so he might not reign, put the land to a tribute of silver and gold, and made Eliakim the son of Josiah king, turning his name to Jehoiakim. Jehoiakim taxed the people to pay Pharaoh, exacting the silver and gold of every man of the land, and he also did evil in the sight of the Lord like his forefathers, not like his father Josiah.

Josiah is eight years old when he begins to reign and reigns thirty one years in Jerusalem, and he does that which is right in the sight of the Lord and walks in the ways of David his father, declining neither to the right hand nor to the left. Comparing the ages shows the point: Manasseh began at twelve, Amon at twenty two, and Josiah at eight, yet the youngest was the wisest. Better is a poor and wise child than an old and foolish king who will no more be admonished. In the eighth year of his reign, while yet young, he begins to seek after the God of David, and in the twelfth year he begins to purge Judah and Jerusalem of the high places, groves, and images. -

They break down the altars of Baal in his presence, cut down the images and groves, and break the carved and molten images to powder, strowing the dust upon the graves of those who had sacrificed to them. He burns the bones of the priests upon their altars and cleanses Judah and Jerusalem, and does the same in the cities of Manasseh, Ephraim, and Simeon, then returns to Jerusalem. -

In the eighteenth year of his reign, when he has purged the land and the house, Josiah sends Shaphan, Maaseiah, and Joah to repair the house of the Lord his God. The money the Levites had gathered from Manasseh, Ephraim, and all the remnant of Israel and Judah is put into the hands of the workmen, who buy hewn stone and timber for couplings and to floor the houses the kings of Judah had destroyed. The men do the work faithfully under overseers of the Levites, with scribes, officers, and porters, that is security, set over the burdens and the service.

When they bring out the money, Hilkiah the priest finds a book of the law of the Lord given by Moses, the very Bible, and delivers it to Shaphan the scribe. Shaphan carries the book to the king and reads it before him, reporting that all committed to the servants is being done and the money delivered to the workmen. -

When the king hears the words of the law, he rends his clothes and commands Hilkiah, Ahikam, Abdon, Shaphan, and Asaiah to go inquire of the Lord for him and for the remnant left in Israel and Judah. He knows great is the wrath of the Lord poured out because the fathers had not kept the word of the Lord to do all that is written in the book. To inquire of the Lord, one must go to a saint, a chosen prophet who has the word. -

Hilkiah and the men go to Huldah the prophetess, wife of Shallum, who dwells in the college in Jerusalem, and she declares the word of the Lord God of Israel. She says the Most High will bring evil and all the curses written in the book upon this place, because they forsook him and burned incense to other gods to provoke him to anger. But because Josiah's heart was tender and he humbled himself, wept, and rent his clothes, the Most High will gather him to his fathers in peace so his eyes will not see the evil to come. -

Josiah gathers all the elders, priests, Levites, and all the people great and small, and reads in their ears all the words of the book of the covenant found in the house of the Lord. He stands in his place and makes a covenant before the Lord to walk after him and keep his commandments, testimonies, and statutes with all his heart and soul, and causes all present to stand to it. Josiah takes away all the abominations out of all the countries belonging to the children of Israel and makes all present serve the Lord their God, and they depart not from following him all his days. All wisdom is the performance of the law.

Josiah keeps a Passover unto the Lord in Jerusalem, and they kill the Passover on the fourteenth day of the first month, keeping the laws pertaining to the Passover. He sets the priests in their charges, encourages them to the service of the house of the Lord, and tells the Levites to put the holy ark in the house Solomon built and to serve the Lord and his people Israel. He commands them to prepare themselves by their courses and stand in the holy place, then kill the Passover, sanctify themselves, and prepare their brethren to do according to the word of the Lord by the hand of Moses. -

Josiah gives the people thirty thousand lambs and kids and three thousand bullocks for the Passover offerings, and his princes give willingly to the people, the priests, and the Levites. The service is prepared, the priests stand in their place and the Levites in their courses, they kill the Passover, sprinkle the blood, flay the offerings, and roast the Passover with fire according to the ordinance. The singers, the sons of Asaph, are in their place according to the commandment of David, and the porters wait at every gate so they need not depart from their service.

All the service of the Lord is prepared the same day to keep the Passover and offer burnt offerings on the altar according to the commandment of king Josiah. The children of Israel present keep the Passover and the feast of unleavened bread seven days, and there was no Passover like it kept in Israel from the days of Samuel the prophet; none of the kings of Israel kept such a Passover as Josiah kept in his eighteenth year.

After this, Necho king of Egypt comes up to fight at Carchemish by Euphrates, and Josiah goes out against him though Necho sends word that his war is not with Josiah and that God had commanded him to make haste. Josiah will not turn his face but disguises himself to fight, hearkening not to the words of Necho from the mouth of God, and the archers shoot him in the valley of Megiddo. His servants take him from the chariot and bring him to Jerusalem, where he dies and is buried, and all Judah and Jerusalem mourn, and Jeremiah laments for Josiah, written in the Lamentations, a book of the Bible.
The rest of the acts of Josiah and his goodness, according to that which is written in the law of the Lord, and his deeds first and last, are written in the book of the kings of Israel and Judah.

These are the commandments, the statutes, and the judgments, commanded to be taught, that thou mightest fear the Lord thy God: the fear always comes up first, thou, and thy son, and thy son's son, all the days of thy life. Hear therefore, O Israel, and observe to do it, that ye may increase mightily. Increase and power are the desire of the people, and keeping the commandments is the one thing our people have not tried; assimilation, the gods of the nations, and politics, liberal or conservative, have all been tried and none of it has worked. The land that floweth with milk and honey is the true riches: cattle, vegetation, agriculture, land to cultivate, the gift that keeps on giving.

Hear, O Israel: the Lord our God is one Lord: and thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thine heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy might. Thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children: diligently means you do not miss a beat. The children are not to be taught the dance challenges, halloween, and the satanic birthdays, and remember that you teach by your actions, so you fix yourself first. Talk of them when thou sittest in thine house: go through the scriptures at home, the histories of Samson, Joseph, Solomon, and David. When thou walkest by the way: when you run into each other, ask, are you keeping the laws, what four chapters did you read today? When thou liest down, and when thou risest up: the bedtime stories are biblical, the ten plagues of Egypt rather than the fairy tales, prayer before they sleep and when they rise, and even the coloring books painting the images brown, bringing it back to its true course.

Thou shalt bind them for a sign upon thine hand, and they shall be as frontlets between thine eyes: bind them in your mind. The commandments are the light, the torch that guides you and leads you in the correct path. And thou shalt write them upon the posts of thy house, and on thy gates.

When the Lord brings thee into great and goodly cities which thou buildedst not, houses full of all good things which thou filledst not, wells digged which thou diggedst not, and thou shalt have eaten and be full, then beware lest thou forget the Lord which brought thee forth out of the house of bondage. Thou shalt fear the Lord thy God, and serve him, and shalt swear by his name; ye shall not go after the gods of the people round about you, for the Lord thy God is a jealous God, lest his anger be kindled and destroy thee from off the face of the earth. Ye shall not tempt the Lord your God, as ye tempted him in Massah.

Ye shall diligently keep the commandments of the Lord your God, and his testimonies, and his statutes. Testimony is one of the trigger words that confuses our people: the laws are what Moses gave, and the testimonies are the history of the forefathers and foremothers, what they went through and how it was handled according to the laws. Everything correlates: when king David had Uriah killed, that goes back to thou shalt not kill, thou shalt not covet, and bearing false witness; he was dealing with much sin in that one matter. That is how you go precept upon precept, line upon line, to the law and to the testimony. A personal testimony that cannot come back to the Bible is not biblical; if they speak not according to this word, it is because there is no light, no truth, in them. Thou shalt do that which is right and good in the sight of the Lord: not by personal standards of what feels good in the heart, but by the standard set before us, for the scripture says plainly that the law is good. The reward is to go in and possess the good land, the real wealth, not the bags and rings and sneakers, which are vanity.

When thy son asketh thee in time to come, saying, what mean the testimonies, and the statutes, and the judgments? The children will ask why David did what he did, why Samson, why Miriam was judged, why Moses was barred; the answer starts with the history. Then thou shalt say unto thy son, we were Pharaoh's bondmen in Egypt, and the Lord brought us out with a mighty hand, and shewed signs and wonders upon Egypt and upon Pharaoh; he brought us out that he might bring us in, to give us the land which he sware unto our fathers. The Most High always keeps his covenant; he is not a man, that he should lie. The Lord commanded us to do all these statutes, to fear the Lord our God, for our good always, that he might preserve us alive: the fear again stands first, and the commandments are for Israel's good and preservation, obligated and not optional, with punishment for breaking and reward for keeping. And it shall be our righteousness, if we observe to do all these commandments: keeping the commandments is what makes you righteous, and righteousness is kept at all times, the fringes worn seven days a week and not on the sabbath only. Words like testimony, righteousness, grace, and faith must be defined out of the scripture itself: the Bible is a dictionary within itself. Egypt means slavery, righteousness means keeping the laws, and going by the Bible's own definitions destroys the private interpretations of the religions.

verses.text: And Hilkiah the high priest said unto Shaphan the scribe, I have found the book of the law in the house of the Lord. And Hilkiah gave the book to Shaphan, and he read it.

And Shaphan the scribe came to the king, and brought the king word again, and said, Thy servants have gathered the money that was found in the house, and have delivered it into the hand of them that do the work, that have the oversight of the house of the Lord.
And Shaphan the scribe shewed the king, saying, Hilkiah the priest hath delivered me a book. And Shaphan read it before the king.
And it came to pass, when the king had heard the words of the book of the law, that he rent his clothes.
And the king commanded Hilkiah the priest, and Ahikam the son of Shaphan, and Achbor the son of Michaiah, and Shaphan the scribe, and Asahiah a servant of the king’s, saying,

Go ye, enquire of the Lord for me, and for the people, and for all Judah, concerning the words of this book that is found: for great is the wrath of the Lord that is kindled against us, because our fathers have not hearkened unto the words of this book, to do according unto all that which is written concerning us.
But to the king of Judah which sent you to enquire of the Lord, thus shall ye say to him, Thus saith the Lord God of Israel, As touching the words which thou hast heard;

Because thine heart was tender, and thou hast humbled thyself before the Lord, when thou heardest what I spake against this place, and against the inhabitants thereof, that they should become a desolation and a curse, and hast rent thy clothes, and wept before me; I also have heard thee, saith the Lord.

Behold therefore, I will gather thee unto thy fathers, and thou shalt be gathered into thy grave in peace; and thine eyes shall not see all the evil which I will bring upon this place. And they brought the king word again.
And the king sent, and they gathered unto him all the elders of Judah and of Jerusalem.

And the king went up into the house of the Lord, and all the men of Judah and all the inhabitants of Jerusalem with him, and the priests, and the prophets, and all the people, both small and great: and he read in their ears all the words of the book of the covenant which was found in the house of the Lord.

And the king stood by a pillar, and made a covenant before the Lord, to walk after the Lord, and to keep his commandments and his testimonies and his statutes with all their heart and all their soul, to perform the words of this covenant that were written in this book. And all the people stood to the covenant.

And the king commanded Hilkiah the high priest, and the priests of the second order, and the keepers of the door, to bring forth out of the temple of the Lord all the vessels that were made for Baal, and for the grove, and for all the host of heaven: and he burned them without Jerusalem in the fields of Kidron, and carried the ashes of them unto Beth–el.

And he put down the idolatrous priests, whom the kings of Judah had ordained to burn incense in the high places in the cities of Judah, and in the places round about Jerusalem; them also that burned incense unto Baal, to the sun, and to the moon, and to the planets, and to all the host of heaven.

And he brought out the grove from the house of the Lord, without Jerusalem, unto the brook Kidron, and burned it at the brook Kidron, and stamped it small to powder, and cast the powder thereof upon the graves of the children of the people.
And he brake down the houses of the sodomites, that were by the house of the Lord, where the women wove hangings for the grove.

And he brought all the priests out of the cities of Judah, and defiled the high places where the priests had burned incense, from Geba to Beer–sheba, and brake down the high places of the gates that were in the entering in of the gate of Joshua the governor of the city, which were on a man’s left hand at the gate of the city.
Nevertheless the priests of the high places came not up to the altar of the Lord in Jerusalem, but they did eat of the unleavened bread among their brethren.
And he defiled Topheth, which is in the valley of the children of Hinnom, that no man might make his son or his daughter to pass through the fire to Molech.

And he took away the horses that the kings of Judah had given to the sun, at the entering in of the house of the Lord, by the chamber of Nathan–melech the chamberlain, which was in the suburbs, and burned the chariots of the sun with fire.

And the altars that were on the top of the upper chamber of Ahaz, which the kings of Judah had made, and the altars which Manasseh had made in the two courts of the house of the Lord, did the king beat down, and brake them down from thence, and cast the dust of them into the brook Kidron.

And the high places that were before Jerusalem, which were on the right hand of the mount of corruption, which Solomon the king of Israel had builded for Ashtoreth the abomination of the Zidonians, and for Chemosh the abomination of the Moabites, and for Milcom the abomination of the children of Ammon, did the king defile.
And he brake in pieces the images, and cut down the groves, and filled their places with the bones of men.
And the king commanded all the people, saying, Keep the passover unto the Lord your God, as it is written in the book of this covenant.
Surely there was not holden such a passover from the days of the judges that judged Israel, nor in all the days of the kings of Israel, nor of the kings of Judah;
But in the eighteenth year of king Josiah, wherein this passover was holden to the Lord in Jerusalem.

Moreover the workers with familiar spirits, and the wizards, and the images, and the idols, and all the abominations that were spied in the land of Judah and in Jerusalem, did Josiah put away, that he might perform the words of the law which were written in the book that Hilkiah the priest found in the house of the Lord.

And like unto him was there no king before him, that turned to the Lord with all his heart, and with all his soul, and with all his might, according to all the law of Moses; neither after him arose there any like him.
Josiah was eight years old when he began to reign, and he reigned in Jerusalem one and thirty years.
And he did that which was right in the sight of the Lord, and walked in the ways of David his father, and declined neither to the right hand, nor to the left.

For in the eighth year of his reign, while he was yet young, he began to seek after the God of David his father: and in the twelfth year he began to purge Judah and Jerusalem from the high places, and the groves, and the carved images, and the molten images.

And they brake down the altars of Baalim in his presence; and the images, that were on high above them, he cut down; and the groves, and the carved images, and the molten images, he brake in pieces, and made dust of them, and strowed it upon the graves of them that had sacrificed unto them.
And he burnt the bones of the priests upon their altars, and cleansed Judah and Jerusalem.
And so did he in the cities of Manasseh, and Ephraim, and Simeon, even unto Naphtali, with their mattocks round about.
And when he had broken down the altars and the groves, and had beaten the graven images into powder, and cut down all the idols throughout all the land of Israel, he returned to Jerusalem.
Moreover Josiah kept a passover unto the Lord in Jerusalem: and they killed the passover on the fourteenth day of the first month.

text.text: And Hilkiah the high priest said unto Shaphan the scribe, I have found the book of the law in the house of the Lord. And Hilkiah gave the book to Shaphan, and he read it.

And Shaphan the scribe came to the king, and brought the king word again, and said, Thy servants have gathered the money that was found in the house, and have delivered it into the hand of them that do the work, that have the oversight of the house of the Lord.
And Shaphan the scribe shewed the king, saying, Hilkiah the priest hath delivered me a book. And Shaphan read it before the king.
And it came to pass, when the king had heard the words of the book of the law, that he rent his clothes.
And the king commanded Hilkiah the priest, and Ahikam the son of Shaphan, and Achbor the son of Michaiah, and Shaphan the scribe, and Asahiah a servant of the king’s, saying,

Go ye, enquire of the Lord for me, and for the people, and for all Judah, concerning the words of this book that is found: for great is the wrath of the Lord that is kindled against us, because our fathers have not hearkened unto the words of this book, to do according unto all that which is written concerning us.
But to the king of Judah which sent you to enquire of the Lord, thus shall ye say to him, Thus saith the Lord God of Israel, As touching the words which thou hast heard;

Because thine heart was tender, and thou hast humbled thyself before the Lord, when thou heardest what I spake against this place, and against the inhabitants thereof, that they should become a desolation and a curse, and hast rent thy clothes, and wept before me; I also have heard thee, saith the Lord.

Behold therefore, I will gather thee unto thy fathers, and thou shalt be gathered into thy grave in peace; and thine eyes shall not see all the evil which I will bring upon this place. And they brought the king word again.
And the king sent, and they gathered unto him all the elders of Judah and of Jerusalem.

And the king went up into the house of the Lord, and all the men of Judah and all the inhabitants of Jerusalem with him, and the priests, and the prophets, and all the people, both small and great: and he read in their ears all the words of the book of the covenant which was found in the house of the Lord.

And the king stood by a pillar, and made a covenant before the Lord, to walk after the Lord, and to keep his commandments and his testimonies and his statutes with all their heart and all their soul, to perform the words of this covenant that were written in this book. And all the people stood to the covenant.

And the king commanded Hilkiah the high priest, and the priests of the second order, and the keepers of the door, to bring forth out of the temple of the Lord all the vessels that were made for Baal, and for the grove, and for all the host of heaven: and he burned them without Jerusalem in the fields of Kidron, and carried the ashes of them unto Beth–el.

And he put down the idolatrous priests, whom the kings of Judah had ordained to burn incense in the high places in the cities of Judah, and in the places round about Jerusalem; them also that burned incense unto Baal, to the sun, and to the moon, and to the planets, and to all the host of heaven.

And he brought out the grove from the house of the Lord, without Jerusalem, unto the brook Kidron, and burned it at the brook Kidron, and stamped it small to powder, and cast the powder thereof upon the graves of the children of the people.
And he brake down the houses of the sodomites, that were by the house of the Lord, where the women wove hangings for the grove.

And he brought all the priests out of the cities of Judah, and defiled the high places where the priests had burned incense, from Geba to Beer–sheba, and brake down the high places of the gates that were in the entering in of the gate of Joshua the governor of the city, which were on a man’s left hand at the gate of the city.
Nevertheless the priests of the high places came not up to the altar of the Lord in Jerusalem, but they did eat of the unleavened bread among their brethren.
And he defiled Topheth, which is in the valley of the children of Hinnom, that no man might make his son or his daughter to pass through the fire to Molech.

And he took away the horses that the kings of Judah had given to the sun, at the entering in of the house of the Lord, by the chamber of Nathan–melech the chamberlain, which was in the suburbs, and burned the chariots of the sun with fire.

And the altars that were on the top of the upper chamber of Ahaz, which the kings of Judah had made, and the altars which Manasseh had made in the two courts of the house of the Lord, did the king beat down, and brake them down from thence, and cast the dust of them into the brook Kidron.

And the high places that were before Jerusalem, which were on the right hand of the mount of corruption, which Solomon the king of Israel had builded for Ashtoreth the abomination of the Zidonians, and for Chemosh the abomination of the Moabites, and for Milcom the abomination of the children of Ammon, did the king defile.
And he brake in pieces the images, and cut down the groves, and filled their places with the bones of men.
And the king commanded all the people, saying, Keep the passover unto the Lord your God, as it is written in the book of this covenant.
Surely there was not holden such a passover from the days of the judges that judged Israel, nor in all the days of the kings of Israel, nor of the kings of Judah;
But in the eighteenth year of king Josiah, wherein this passover was holden to the Lord in Jerusalem.

And like unto him was there no king before him, that turned to the Lord with all his heart, and with all his soul, and with all his might, according to all the law of Moses; neither after him arose there any like him.
